<a name="DxfViewer+Load"></a>

### dxfViewer.Load(params)
Load DXF into the viewer. Old content is discarded, state is reset.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>DxfViewer</code>](#DxfViewer)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| params | <code>object</code> |  |
| params.url | <code>string</code> | DXF file URL. |
| params.fonts | <code>Array.&lt;string&gt;</code> | List of font URLs. Files should have typeface.js format.  Fonts are used in the specified order, each one is checked until necessary glyph is found.  Text is not rendered if fonts are not specified. |
| params.progressCbk | <code>function</code> | (phase, processedSize, totalSize)  Possible phase values:  * "font"  * "fetch"  * "parse"  * "prepare" |
| params.workerFactory | <code>function</code> | Factory for worker creation. The worker script  should invoke DxfViewer.SetupWorker() function. |

<a name="DxfViewer+Render"></a>

### dxfViewer.Render()
Draw the current scene into the canvas. The viewer renders on its own whenever the view
 or the layer visibility changes, so this is only needed after modifying the scene
 returned by GetScene().

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>DxfViewer</code>](#DxfViewer)

<a name="DxfViewer+SetClearColor"></a>

### dxfViewer.SetClearColor(color)
Change the frame buffer clear color. Unlike the `clearColor` option of the same name, this
 takes effect immediately: the already loaded scene is re-rendered with the new background
 and the entity colors are corrected against it again. Safe to call before anything is
 loaded, where it only establishes the background color.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>DxfViewer</code>](#DxfViewer)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| color | <code>number</code> \| <code>string</code> \| <code>three.Color</code> | New clear color. The alpha value is not changed, see      the `clearAlpha` option. |

<a name="DxfViewer+Subscribe"></a>

### dxfViewer.Subscribe(eventName, eventHandler)
Subscribe to the specified event. The following events are defined:
 * "loaded" - new scene loaded.
 * "cleared" - current scene cleared.
 * "destroyed" - viewer instance destroyed.
 * "resized" - viewport size changed. Details: {width, height}
 * "pointerdown" - Details: {domEvent, position:{x,y}}, position is in scene coordinates.
 * "pointerup"
 * "viewChanged"
 * "message" - Some message from the viewer. {message: string, level: string}.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>DxfViewer</code>](#DxfViewer)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eventName | <code>string</code> |  |
| eventHandler | <code>function</code> | Accepts event object. |

<a name="DxfViewer+Unsubscribe"></a>

### dxfViewer.Unsubscribe(eventName, eventHandler)
Unsubscribe from previously subscribed event. The arguments should match previous
Subscribe() call.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>DxfViewer</code>](#DxfViewer)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| eventName | <code>string</code> | 
| eventHandler | <code>function</code> |

<a name="Pattern+isQcadDefault"></a>

### pattern.isQcadDefault
Whether this definition has the shape QCAD writes into every hatch it exports: one solid
line at 45 degrees, regardless of the pattern the entity names. It is the only shape an
embedded definition is ever doubted for, and on its own it settles nothing - ANSI31 is that
line - so `ContradictsNamedPattern()` decides what to do about it.

**Kind**: instance property of [<code>Pattern</code>](#Pattern)  
<a name="Pattern+ContradictsNamedPattern"></a>

### pattern.ContradictsNamedPattern(named) ⇒ <code>boolean</code>
Check whether the shape of this pattern contradicts the shape of `named`, i.e. whether the
two cannot be the same pattern. Used to tell a placeholder definition embedded by an editor
from a real one, so only the properties an embedded definition preserves are compared: the
number of lines, the angles between them and the signs of the dash sequences. Spacing, base
points and dash lengths are all scaled by the embedding and so say nothing about the name.

The angles are compared relative to the pattern's own first line, not to the drawing, because
an embedded definition carries the orientation the drawing uses the pattern in. A mirrored
plan hatches "ANSI31" along 135 degrees and one of its walls rotates that by another 90, so
its definition lines read 45 - which against the pattern table's own 45 is either the same
pattern or half a turn from it, depending on which of the two rotations is accounted for.
Comparing the internal structure sidesteps the question, and a placeholder is a single line
at 135 where the name means three horizontal ones, so the line count still separates them.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>Pattern</code>](#Pattern)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| named | [<code>Pattern</code>](#Pattern) | Pattern to compare with, normally the one found by name. |

<a name="RegisterPattern"></a>

## RegisterPattern(pattern, isMetric)
Add a pattern to the registry its name is looked up in.

**Kind**: global function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pattern | [<code>Pattern</code>](#Pattern) | Must be named; an anonymous pattern throws. |
| isMetric | <code>boolean</code> | Register in the metric registry when true, the imperial one when  false. The two are selected by the drawing's $MEASUREMENT variable. |

<a name="LookupPattern"></a>

## LookupPattern(name, isMetric) ⇒ [<code>Pattern</code>](#Pattern)
Find a registered pattern by name, case-insensitively.

**Kind**: global function  
**Returns**: [<code>Pattern</code>](#Pattern) - Null if no pattern of that name is registered.  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | <code>string</code> | Pattern name. |
| isMetric | <code>boolean</code> | Which registry to search. See RegisterPattern(). |
